This verse anchors Cyril's theology of redemptive suffering both for Christ and for those united to Him.

Cyril of Alexandria Commentary on the Gospel of John (c. 428 AD)

'I am come a light into the world, that whosoever believeth on me should not abide in darkness' Cyril reads as the final Johannine 'I am' statement before the Passion narrative begins — recapitulating the prologue's light-darkness imagery now grounded in the incarnate Christ's completed public ministry. The 'not abide in darkness' (mē meinē — subjunctive negative) Cyril takes as both promise and warning: the choice to abide in darkness is human refusal, not divine fate. Christ's coming as Light is for ALL; whether one walks in that Light is conditioned on faith. The verse provides the textual transition from public ministry (chapters 1-12) to the Farewell Discourses (chapters 13-17) in the Gospel's structure.
